topic: Enhanced recovery compliance in oesophago-gastric cancer surgery
standard: Enhanced recovery programme (ERP) elements: mobilisation, oral intake, NGT removal, drain removal
finding: Site A: mobilisation 25%, oral intake 19%, NGT 65%, drain removal 69%. Site B: mobilisation 51%, NGT removal 37%, drain removal 15%, oral intake 47%
change: Collaborative QI with workshops and meetings assessing ERP variation, prospective compliance recording and cross-site feedback

detail.setting: Two oesophago-gastric cancer centres (sites A and B)

cycle1.result: Site A: mobilisation 25%, oral intake 19%, NGT 65%, drain removal 69%. Site B: mobilisation 51%, NGT removal 37%, drain removal 15%, oral intake 47%

detail.intervention: Collaborative QI with workshops and meetings assessing ERP variation, prospective compliance recording and cross-site feedback

cycle2.result: Site A: mobilisation 28% (P = 0.448), oral intake 56% (P = 0.002), NGT 54%, drain removal 53%. Site B: mobilisation 68% (P = 0.097), NGT removal 51%, drain removal 32%, oral intake 34%

detail.other_findings: Site A pneumonia fell 47% to 22% (P = 0.024) and length of stay 11 to 9 days (P = 0.024); site B length of stay 12 to 14 days. Lack of standard ERP definitions was a challenge.
